shape_hint: A pin bent from half-round wire: the two flat faces lie together to form a round shank of diameter d, a loop (eye) of outside diameter c and length b at one end, and two legs of unequal length (the longer one projects by a) that are spread apart after insertion through the cross hole.

role_map.row label: nominal size = diameter of the split pin hole
role_map.d_max: maximum diameter d of the closed shank (both half-round legs together): "d max" (globalfastener), second of "d min/max" (fasten.it), "Shank diameter max" (woodstock), "Maximum Pin Diameter" (amesweb)
role_map.a_max: maximum extension a of the longer leg beyond the shorter one

notes: All 16 nominal sizes 0.6-20 and the five dimension columns are kept; the two application columns are dropped. Candidate 16 x 7 -> kept 16 x 5. Clusters: globalfastener (ISO 1234-1997 and DIN EN ISO 1234-1998 pages; fullerfasteners is the same template), fasten.it (DIN EN ISO 1234 sheet), fasteners.eu group (a max, b, c; digipich prints c and a as "<= x"), schrauben-lexikon (b, c max, sizes 1-16), RoyMech (b and the c range, sizes 0.8-13), woodstockindustrial (shank diameter max, sizes 1-13) and the amesweb calculator (all columns, all sizes). amesweb and RoyMech are engineering reference sites, not sellers. Thinnest cells: d max at 0.6, 0.8, 16 and 20 has exactly globalfastener + fasten.it + amesweb. Edition trap: c max at nominal 20 is 38.5 on every ISO 1234-labelled page counted here, but 38.6 on the DIN 94 pages of globalfastener and fasten.it and on the fullerfasteners "ISO 1234" page (not counted: copy of the globalfastener template carrying the DIN number). a min (0.8 ... 3.15) and c min are also printed by globalfastener and amesweb; schrauben-lexikon prints a min 3.2 where they print 3.15. Nominal size is the split pin hole diameter, not the pin diameter. Lengths are a separate series and are not in this table.
